position_start: the base carries no position at the start of the period

subject: gov.policy
name: National Digital Payments Strategy 2026-2030
position_end: Proposes the first outbound cross-border transfers, against 18.5tn birr a year

note: proposes first-ever outbound cross-border transfers against 18.5tn birr a year in digital transactions

subject: gov.policy
name: National Digital Transformation Council
position_end: Holds that the programme is to be judged on lives changed, with no published measure behind it
note: restated that the digital programme is to be judged on lives changed rather than systems deployed — a measurement claim with no published measure behind it

subject: gov.policy
name: Telecom liberalisation
milestone: Monopoly ended 2021; one new full licensee since
position_end: Two operators; the argument has moved to whether the state is provider or regulator
note: ended the Ethio Telecom monopoly in 2021 with Safaricom the only new full licensee; the debate has moved to whether the state acts as provider or as regulator and partner

subject: gov.legislate
name: Berne Convention accession
milestone: Draft ratification proclamation before the Council of Ministers, reported 2026-08-01
position_end: Draft ratification proclamation submitted to the Council of Ministers; Ethiopia not yet a party
note: reported by the Authority rather than from the instrument; the draft proclamation is not held and no parliamentary date is published

subject: gov.legislate
name: Copyright Proclamation 410/2004 online-infringement amendment
milestone: Drafting with Addis Ababa University School of Law reported 2026-08-01, after several consultation rounds
position_end: Draft would add internet service provider duties, procedures for blocking infringing sites and a rights-holder take-down notice to the 2004 proclamation
note: the first platform-liability instrument in the base for Ethiopia; no draft text, no timetable and no introduction date published, and enforcement is rights-holder-initiated by URL because channel operators cannot be identified, against existing remedies of one-to-ten-year sentences and fines up to 25,000 Birr

subject: gov.legislate
name: Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity Proclamation No. 1426/2026
status: Implemented, with a transition period before full compliance
milestone: Signed by President Taye Atske Selassie at Addis Ababa 2026-07-21; art.28 sets commencement one year after gazettement (about July 2027)
position_end: 12 critical sectors designated, 18 core obligations on owners and operators, and a Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity Fund; art.28 sets a one-year transition to commencement after gazettement (about July 2027); the Council of Ministers and INSA hold regulation-making powers under arts.26-27
note: the twelve sectors are ICT, financial services, security and public safety, transport, education, health, water and energy, government services, emergency and disaster response, agriculture, trade and commerce, and industry; INSA is to write sector-specific standards and guidelines, provide technical assistance and enforce during a transition period whose length the briefing does not state, and the ratification, assent and commencement dates are not established in the base

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital Identification Proclamation 1284/2023
milestone: Gazetted 18 April 2023, Federal Negarit Gazette No. 19
position_end: The statute behind the national digital identity, establishing a foundational identification system for the registration of residents, the right of a resident to be identified, a registration system for personal data and the issuance of a unique number, and creating the institution that runs it
note: the held text is the English operative column of a bilingual gazette, complete through article 26; the Amharic column did not survive extraction, and no implementing regulation under the proclamation is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Ethiopian Statistical Service Proclamation
status: Enacted, approved by the House on 30 June 2026 with no gazette text located
position_start: the 2005 proclamation establishing the Central Statistics Authority as an autonomous federal agency
position_end: a successor proclamation approved by the House of People's Representatives, intended to strengthen the statistics service's independence
note: no gazette text or proclamation number had been located at the probe date

subject: gov.legislate
name: Judicial review of licence revocation without court order
milestone: Federal High Court of Lideta ruling 2026-06-22
position_end: December 2025 decree struck down; revocation without a court order held unconstitutional
note: the Federal High Court of Lideta struck down a December 2025 lottery-administration decree cutting banking services to betting platforms and gateways, finding licence revocation without a court order unconstitutional and noting that suspicion does not constitute guilt; by 2025 online sports betting was more than 99% of all Ethiopian gateway volume

subject: gov.legislate
name: Prohibition of virtual assets
position_end: The whole category prohibited absent express authorisation; no new rule, no enforcement mechanism
note: a central-bank public notice widened the prohibition to the whole category by clarification rather than by new rule — use, purchase, sale, exchange, transfer, trading, settlement and facilitation prohibited absent express authorisation, with custody and administration named; no new regulation and no enforcement mechanism was announced

subject: gov.legislate
name: Tax assessment of payment gateways
movement: Advanced, as an enforcement action rather than as policy
position_end: Three-year throughput restated from ETB 32bn to 143.9bn and taxed; corrected data refused
note: the central bank conflated gross transaction volume with gateway revenue in data compiled for a revenue audit, restating one gateway's three-year throughput of ETB 32bn as ETB 143.9bn and taxing the difference at 30%; corrected datasets issued in April 2026 were not accepted, ETB 818m was swept from frozen accounts in May 2026 against a liability counsel puts at ETB 20-30m, with parallel sweeps against two other gateways; the overstatement is more than ETB 111bn, against a gateway commission of about 2.5% split with the state operator

subject: gov.legislate
name: Telecommunications Licensing Directive 792/2021
position_end: In force; unified operator licences awarded by competitive bidding and valid fifteen years
note: the framework a third operator or a satellite licence would be issued under: two individual licences — unified telecommunications service and internet exchange point — granted by auction, beauty contest or a hybrid, and thirteen class licences including internet service provider, data centre, hosting, VSAT and GMPCS landing rights; individual and class licences run fifteen years, renewable for a further fifteen

subject: gov.protect
name: Data request to diplomatic missions
position_end: A foreign ministry note asking all accredited diplomatic missions and international and regional organisations to submit lists and addresses of every Ethiopian and foreign employee without diplomatic privileges, together with tenant and landlord details
note: no legal basis, retention rule, data controller or purpose limitation is stated in the note as reported

subject: gov.protect
name: Data sharing arrangement under the health memorandum
milestone: Provided for at 2.5.2, still to be negotiated
position_end: The two governments intend to negotiate an arrangement for exchanging data on the memorandum's long-term performance and for accountability to the United States Congress, expected to run two years beyond the five-year term; a rights organisation's reading of the seven signed memoranda puts Ethiopia among five whose text requires unilateral sharing of specimens and pathogen-sequencing data, and all seven as requiring broad audit access. No text is published, and the State Department briefly posted a subset in March 2026, then removed access
note: 4.7 makes failure to fulfil the specimen and data sharing arrangements grounds for changing or discontinuing assistance, although the memorandum creates no specimen arrangement

subject: gov.protect
name: Development Bank of Ethiopia Information Disclosure Policy
milestone: Policy adopted classifying client credit information, legal case files, strategy papers, security protocols and third-party contracts as permanently non-disclosable, reported 2026-08-08
position_end: In force: client credit information and other named categories are exempt from declassification where disclosure could cause substantial harm to the Bank, its stakeholders or national interest; the Bank may also decline requests requiring it to create records it does not already hold
note: part of a wider reform push under new president Esayas Kassa and EIH chair Brook Taye; no legal instrument number, gazette reference or appeal mechanism is stated

subject: gov.protect
name: Independent data-protection safeguards over the national digital identity
milestone: Absence set out in a public critique, 2026-08-09
position_end: Not held
note: a published critique argues the identity system risks becoming an instrument of mass profiling in the absence of independent data-protection impact assessments, meaningful citizen rights and legal limits on state access; the base holds no such assessment, no redress mechanism and no statutory access limit, against 46.5m registrations by July 2026 and a 90m target

subject: gov.protect
name: Personal Data Protection Proclamation 1321/2024
position_end: In force; directives still unissued and the Authority has yet to enforce
note: a comprehensive regime with extraterritorial reach designating the Ethiopian Communications Authority as regulator; a year on the secondary directives remain unissued, public awareness is low and the Authority has yet to enforce, while the identity system authenticates about 4m times a day across more than 150 agencies

subject: gov.protect
name: Secondary directives under the data-protection law
milestone: Four directives stated to be months from approval, November 2025
position_end: The communications authority, which enforces the proclamation, states that four directives are expected to be approved in the coming months as it expands its technical capacity and staffing, and has previewed a digital portal for data controllers and processors to register - an early step towards a national register of them
note: the directives are not published, the portal is a preview shown at a workshop co-hosted with a vendor, and no approval date or draft text is stated; a year after the proclamation took effect nothing has been enforced under it

subject: gov.regional
name: Digital identity cooperation with Zambia
position_end: Identity cooperation agreed
sources: 2026-03-24 Zambia looking for MOSIP system integrator to support digital ID project

subject: gov.regional
name: Digital public infrastructure export to Mozambique
milestone: Three-year memorandum signed at Addis Ababa 2026-04-27
position_end: Digital-ID, DPI-pilot, interoperability and cybersecurity support to Mozambique, with a joint working group
sources: 2026-04-27-mozambique-ethiopia-mou-digital-identity-clubofmozambique|2026-04-28 Mozambique taps Ethiopia's digital ID expertise in DPI partnership
note: an initial three-year memorandum, extendable by consent, signed at Addis Ababa on 2026-04-27 between Mozambique's Digital Transformation and Innovation Agency and Faydaverse Digital Solutions Enterprise, under which the Ethiopian side provides digital-ID, DPI-pilot, interoperability and joint-cybersecurity support and a joint working group coordinates implementation; the held trade-press account dated the signing 2026-04-28, its own publication date

subject: gov.regional
name: Horizon Fiber terrestrial corridor
milestone: Active deployment entered, architecture finalised and site materials procured (2026-08)
position_end: In active deployment: end-to-end solution architecture finalised and site-material procurement complete on a multi-terabit terrestrial corridor linking Djibouti, Ethiopia, Sudan and Jeddah
note: the Ethio Telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel memorandum of December 2024 became binding in February 2026 and entered active deployment by August, extending the stated route to Saudi Arabia's Jeddah; no route length, capacity figure, cost, in-service date or transit-revenue projection is published, so the transit-hub claim rests on the corridor's geography alone. One of the four territories it crosses is at war

subject: gov.regional
name: Regional legal harmonisation commitments
position_start: ratification of the 2023 regional treaty, the operative instrument for Ethiopia's standing in the regional harmonisation framework
position_end: that treaty plus a ministerial communique on labour and migration and a completed continental free trade implementation review intended to guide domestic regulatory alignment

subject: gov.standards
name: Ethiopian eGovernment Interoperability Framework
position_end: Still in development

subject: gov.standards
name: MOSIP open-source identity platform
position_end: The reference implementation the wider ecosystem points to
sources: 2026-07-07 Beyond the Platform Understanding the Growing MOSIP Ecosystem
note: Fayda is the flagship MOSIP deployment and the reference implementation the wider ecosystem points to; modular open-source under MPL 2.0, incubated at IIIT-Bangalore

subject: gov.standards
name: National Livestock Data Standards
position_end: Endorsed, with more than 300 experts and collectors trained
note: developed with the ministry and endorsed, then cascaded on a training-of-trainers model with more than 300 experts and data collectors trained

subject: gov.discourse
name: Climate information integrity project
position_end: A project on climate-change disinformation and information integrity in African digital ecosystems, focused on Uganda and Ethiopia and supported by a UNESCO-led global initiative, combining research mapping how climate disinformation spreads and who drives it with a fact-checking masterclass at the 2026 internet-freedom forum, online training for journalists and civil society, and tracking of African governments' communications ahead of the November 2026 climate conference
note: no budget or duration is stated

subject: finance.budget
name: Audit of digital spending for any in-scope year

subject: finance.budget
name: Federal appropriation for digital transformation
movement: Advanced, mostly the birr float rather than real growth
position_end: ETB 9.05bn for FY2026/27, dominated by the AI university line
note: 34 budget lines across FY2024/25 to FY2026/27: ETB 1,206,492,295 appropriated in FY2024/25 against an outturn of ETB 1,526,775,873, ETB 3,754,558,918 in FY2025/26 and ETB 9,049,102,733 in FY2026/27; the year-on-year rise is mostly the birr float rather than real growth, and the FY2026/27 total is dominated by the AI university line; the digital lines sit inside a federal budget of 2.34 trillion birr for FY2026/27, ratified 2026-07-07 and up 21.3% on the year before, and the three digital totals round to ETB 1.21bn, 3.75bn and 9.05bn

subject: finance.budget
name: Published budget execution for FY2025/26
position_end: H1 FY2025/26: ETB 704.7bn mobilised, 48.1% of the annual target, against ETB 798.2bn spent, 48.3% of the approved budget
note: the Ministry describes it as the second in a 2025/26 series of fiscal disclosures, so the cadence resumed before this file rather than at it; recurrent spending ran at 39.3% of its budget against 62.9% of the capital budget, and direct budget support from development partners at ETB 67.8bn, 28.8% of the ETB 235.5bn projected for the year

subject: finance.mou
name: Debt treatment under the G20 Common Framework

position_end: that memorandum being implemented — a bilateral agreement with Italy and an agreement in principle with bondholders on the 2024 notes

subject: finance.new
name: Corruption allegations against a donor-funded digital project

position_end: Allegations of fraud in development assistance touching a German-funded digital project were raised in the federal parliament, with a demand that they be investigated to a conclusion

subject: finance.new
name: Digitally enabled pluralistic extension services programme (FAO)
position_end: US$300,000 FAO grant (2026-2028) converting a catalytic start-up initiative into a long-term programme delivering agricultural extension services through digital channels

name: Ethio Telecom public share offer
position_end: 10% distributed through Telebirr

name: World Bank Digital ID for Inclusion Project
position_start: US$350m approved, with no disbursement or performance rating on file

sources: 2026-05-18 WB Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project - implementation support mission aide-memoire|2023-11-20 WB Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project - project appraisal document|2023-12-13-wb-eth-001-ethiopia-digital-id-for-inclusion-and|2024-01-01-nidp-fayda-90m-by-2028-world-bank-project-page

subject: infra.connect
name: Addis Ababa Internet Exchange
position_start: the country's first internet exchange, operating for over a year at a data centre in the technology park
position_end: the same exchange measured: three members, 21 Gbps of cumulative port capacity, all three peering at the route server and two of three using route origin validation

subject: infra.connect
name: Ethio Telecom network
position_end: The 2026/27 business plan raises mobile network capacity from 115.1 million to 135.7 million subscribers, 4G capacity from 22.79 million to 35.31 million and 5G capacity from 1.41 million to 2.70 million; 4G sites rise to 11,014 with population coverage from 82.23 to 95 per cent and geographic coverage from 36.3 to 54 per cent, towns with 4G from 1,200 to 1,500, 5G sites from 340 to 648 and 5G towns from 33 to 73. Backbone fibre grows from 23,442 km to 25,642 km and international gateway and cache capacity from 4.3 Tbps to 5.2 Tbps, with 1,685 new mobile sites including 605 rural sites reaching more than 1,400 kebeles and 4.5 million people; data-centre IT load rises from 5 MW to 6.24 MW and 624 to 752 racks. The revenue target is ETB 295 billion
note: a plan rather than an outturn: every figure above the current level is a target the operator set itself, and the base holds no independent verification of the current levels either

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile data pricing
position_start: mobile data priced, on the operator's own account, below cost and among the lowest in Africa
position_end: prices raised by between 20 and 82 percent across most plans from 23 December 2025, with data volumes cut on several packages
note: the market assessment's affordability figures are not present in the captured excerpt

subject: infra.connect
name: Network expansion contracts from MWC 2026
milestone: Ethio Telecom-ZTE progress review 2026-08-10: 879 sites completed under the ZTE programme
position_end: Ericsson 1,500 sites and 502 upgrades under the MWC contracts; separately, 879 sites completed under the ZTE programme (462 RAN modernisation, 237 microwave-link upgrades, 103 IP RAN sites), 92% 4G population coverage across ZTE's own network footprint, with 124 new sites, 272 U2100 refarming sites and 115 rural sites still to come
note: Ericsson 1,500 mobile sites and 502 3G-to-4G upgrades, ZTE 647 sites taking 4G population coverage to 95.5%, plus Huawei and Nokia, under the Next Horizon: Digital and Beyond 2028 strategy; the 2026-08-10 ZTE progress review's 92% coverage figure is scoped to ZTE's own network footprint, not reconciled against the MWC-contract account's 95.5% national 4G population-coverage figure

subject: infra.connect
name: Next Horizon: Digital & Beyond 2028 strategy
milestone: First year of the three-year strategy completed
position_end: The incumbent operator completed the first year of its three-year strategy on 3 September 2026, putting its customer base at about 90 million and its mobile money users at close to 61 million, and set second-year targets of 96.2 million customers by the end of 2026/27, 4G population coverage of 95 per cent from 82.23 per cent, 4G service in 1,500 towns and 5G in 73 towns, with more than 2.6 million jobs claimed by 2027/28
note: the operator's own account of its own strategy, with no independent measure of the first-year outturn against the targets it was set

subject: infra.connect
name: Safaricom Ethiopia second network
position_end: The second network passed 15 million 90-day active subscribers in under four years of commercial operation, announced on the fifth anniversary of its unified licence of 9 July 2021; commercial service began in October 2022. It has deployed more than 3,500 network sites, all 4G-enabled and 5G-ready, reaching about 60 per cent of the population, and says the growing customer base is moving the business towards breakeven. It puts community investment at ETB 139 million directly and a further ETB 545 million from shareholders and partners, ETB 684 million over four years
note: the operator's own figures, including the subscriber definition; breakeven is stated as a direction rather than a date, and no revenue or loss figure accompanies it

subject: infra.connect
name: Safaricom regional fibre deployment
position_end: Under construction, Afdera to Mekelle

subject: infra.connect

position_end: Live

subject: infra.store
name: Government business continuity and disaster recovery
position_start: neither a business continuity plan nor a disaster recovery plan in place, on the government's own 2023 assessment
position_end: no stated plan, but in-country capacity to host one — a new private cloud platform and the incumbent operator's Tier III data-centre expansion

subject: infra.store
name: Wingu Cloud Exchange in-country cloud
position_end: Compute, Kubernetes and storage priced in birr, hybrid with Azure and AWS
sources: 2026-04-01 Wingu Africa debuts cloud exchange platform in Ethiopia

subject: infra.energy
name: Bitdeer Oromia bitcoin-mining site
position_end: 40 MW operating with 20 MW in progress
sources: 2026-01-12 Bitdeer completes 40 MW Oromia bitcoin-mining site in Ethiopia
note: 40 MW complete with 20 MW more in progress; a company that had weighed Nigeria for a similar project relocated it here on far cheaper electricity

subject: infra.energy
name: Ethio Telecom Green Operator renewable network programme
milestone: 39.72 MW of installed solar at 2026-08-04, up 12.72 MW over the financial year
position_start: 27 MW installed solar at the FY2024/25 close, derived
position_end: 39.72 MW installed solar across 190 fully solar-powered sites, 867 hybrid solar-and-battery systems and 1,114 lithium-ion storage units, with diesel generator running time down by up to 40%
note: the operator's own unaudited figures, disclosed alongside the eighth Green Legacy tree-planting round and tied to serving rural and off-grid communities; the last financial year added 215 solar-powered sites and modernised 774 base stations, and the start figure is derived by subtracting that year's 12.72 MW from the 39.72 MW total

subject: infra.cybersec
name: INSA cybersecurity and sovereign-cloud foundations
position_end: Sovereign cloud and forensic laboratory stated in the strategy, not built

note: the October 2025 integration linked M-PESA to more than 30 banks and wallets with real-time transfers and EthQR merchant payments across 50,000+ merchants; interoperability rather than licensing is the growth lever

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Integration of school data into the national education information system
position_start: an education information system operating at decentralised levels, with no stated route from school data into it
position_end: an adopted open-source education system explicitly aimed at operationalising the national system at local level, and funded integration of all 57 refugee primary schools into it

name: Integration of social protection into the whole-of-government data exchange

position_end: that requirement plus a funded successor safety-net project committing to stronger digital tools and improved monitoring behind delivery

subject: dpi.exchange
name: National data exchange platform

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Socioeconomic impact measurement of digital public infrastructure
position_end: A pilot measuring the socioeconomic impacts of digital public infrastructure, with results and a stated way forward

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Tax administration diagnostic assessment
position_end: An international diagnostic across nine performance outcome areas finds the absence of a robust integrated tax administration information system adversely affecting the registered taxpayer base, with online registration and updating of taxpayer information sought, electronic payment facilities not in place and use of electronic filing assessed as an indicator in its own right
note: an official-use diagnostic; the per-indicator grades are in the report and no earlier assessment is held to compare them against

subject: dpi.id

position_end: 2,000 of 6,000 planned distributed, about US$17m, with 4,000 re-tendered

subject: dpi.id

note: reported by the lender’s mission, not by the programme; no award or supplier is on record

subject: dpi.pay
